html:
A satellite news channel launched in Doha, Qatar, in 1996, which broke the hold of governments over Arab television news. Its name means "the peninsula".

Until then most Arabs watched state channels that praised their rulers. Qatar's emir, Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, who had just taken power, paid for a channel that would be different, and hired many staff from a BBC Arabic television service that had shut down. Al Jazeera ran live debates in which Islamists, liberals, Israelis and opposition figures argued on air, and it reported on governments that had never faced such coverage. Many Arab states banned its reporters or recalled their ambassadors.

After the September 11 attacks it became known worldwide for airing tapes from Osama bin Laden and for its coverage of the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq. In the Arab Spring of 2011 it gave the uprisings huge reach. Critics say it favours Qatar's friends, such as the Muslim Brotherhood, and rarely looks hard at Qatar itself. In 2017 Saudi Arabia and its allies demanded its closure as a condition for lifting their blockade of Qatar.

The network added Al Jazeera English in 2006 and many other channels.
sum: A satellite news channel launched in Doha, Qatar, in 1996, which broke the hold of governments over Arab television news. Its name means "the peninsula".
